from pypdf import PdfReader

patterns=['code','seed','initializ','bound','outlier','checkpoint','grid search','decay','github']
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages):
 text=page.extract_text()
 hits=[]
 for line in text.splitlines():
  if any(re.search(p,line,re.I) for p in patterns):
   hits.append(line)

  print(f'PAGE {i+1}')
  print('\\n'.join(hits))

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem: forecasting pretraining loss early enough to select hyperparameters directly on the target model. The token-position decomposition offers an interpretable empirical perspective on learning dynamics.

The experiments include two model sizes trained for 400B tokens, both in-distribution and out-of-distribution validation, and extrapolation from several training prefixes. Figures 1, 4, and 6 support the positional loss patterns, while the forecasting experiments provide evidence beyond in-sample curve fitting.

The data-mixture application reports consistent perplexity improvements and gains on 12 of 14 model–benchmark combinations. The manuscript provides explicit forecasting equations, and the appendix documents architectures, major training hyperparameters, package versions, and weighting strategies.
weaknesses: The central baseline comparison has an unresolved correctness problem. Table 1 reports in-sample power-law R² values around −2.4 to −2.9 after least-squares fitting to the complete trajectories. The stated family, L=(p1x)^p2+p3, includes a constant mean predictor through p2=0 and an appropriate p3, yielding R²=0. Such strongly negative results suggest failed optimization, undisclosed constraints, or inconsistent evaluation. They cannot substantiate the claimed failure of power laws. Properly optimized refits and documented fitting procedures are essential.

The benefit of positional decomposition is not isolated from incorporating the learning-rate schedule. Once a0 and a1 are frozen, Equation 10 reduces to a constant offset plus the schedule-shaped a2 term. A crucial missing comparison is the same logarithmic/cosine construction fitted directly to aggregate loss with access to the same schedule information. Moreover, no separate runs are identified for developing the functional forms versus evaluating forecasts. Results under one 400B-token cosine schedule and one context length leave the broader forecasting claim insufficiently validated.

The hyperparameter-selection evidence is promising but does not establish reliable ranking. Forecasting is evaluated using 10–40% of training, whereas mixture selection uses only 10B of 400B tokens, or 2.5%. Predicted and realized losses for all five candidates, or another direct assessment of ranking accuracy, are missing. The ID perplexity gains are 0.05–0.07 without uncertainty estimates; averaging five final checkpoints does not measure variation across training runs. Appendix B.2 also selects candidates using benchmark performance without describing a separate final evaluation split.

Important reproduction details remain unspecified: nonlinear solver settings, initialization and parameter constraints, the outlier-removal threshold, checkpoint sampling frequency, the number of mixture-search trials, and the actual candidate and selected mixture weights. No fitting-code or loss-trajectory release is identified. These omissions matter particularly because the method depends on several nonlinear fits and an extrapolated separation point.

The interpretation of positional weighting exceeds the evidence. Equation 17 follows from explicitly freezing a0 and a1 in Equation 8; it is not an independent theoretical justification for uniform weighting. Figure 6 supplies useful empirical support for approximately uniform loss decreases, but that observation does not establish which weighting optimizes training. Three fixed suppression strategies introduced only after the separation point support a limited experimental conclusion about those strategies.

The novelty framing needs correction. Claims that temporal loss modeling is unexplored conflict with the manuscript’s own acknowledgment of prior loss-versus-training-step scaling in Section 3.3. The contribution should be positioned around the positional decomposition and forecasting procedure. The introduction also incorrectly describes power-law behavior as exponential. Overall, the unresolved baseline validity and reproduction issues require substantive revision before a clear Findings recommendation.
